subject: B
topic: All topics of GK & Current Affairs India (mixed)

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Chipko Movement' of the 1970s originated in which present-day state?
questions.explanation: The Chipko Movement started in Chamoli district of present-day Uttarakhand in 1973 when villagers hugged trees to prevent logging. Himachal Pradesh is wrong because the movement originated in Garhwal region, not HP. Jharkhand is wrong as it is in eastern India and associated with tribal movements, not forest conservation in the Himalayas. Chhattisgarh is wrong as it is in central India with no connection to this movement.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about India's foreign trade policy:

(i) India's Foreign Trade Policy (FTP) 2023 has no fixed expiry date.
(ii) The Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) is the implementing agency.
(iii) The FTP 2023 merged MEIS and SEIS into one scheme called RoDTEP.
(iv) Districts as Export Hubs (DEH) initiative is part of FTP 2023.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: FTP 2023 is open-ended with no fixed expiry (i correct), DGFT implements it (ii correct), and DEH is part of FTP 2023 (iv correct). Statement (iii) is wrong because MEIS was replaced by RoDTEP in 2021 under a separate notification, not by FTP 2023 — and SEIS was discontinued separately. RoDTEP was not introduced by FTP 2023.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India has a parliamentary form of government at the Centre and in the states.
Reason (R): In a parliamentary system, the executive is collectively responsible to the legislature and can be removed by a vote of no-confidence.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: India does follow a parliamentary form at both Centre and state levels (A is correct). In a parliamentary system, the executive derives its legitimacy from and is accountable to the legislature through collective responsibility (R is correct). R directly explains why India's system is classified as parliamentary — the defining feature is executive accountability to the legislature. Option 2 is wrong because R is indeed the defining characteristic that explains A. Option 3 is wrong because R is factually correct. Option 4 is wrong because A is factually correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following Indian classical dances with their states of origin:

Column I:
(a) Mohiniyattam
(b) Sattriya
(c) Manipuri
(d) Kuchipudi

Column II:
(i) Andhra Pradesh
(ii) Assam
(iii) Manipur
(iv) Kerala

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Mohiniyattam is from Kerala (iv), Sattriya from Assam (ii) originated in Vaishnavite monasteries, Manipuri from Manipur (iii), and Kuchipudi from Andhra Pradesh (i). Option 2 is wrong because it pairs Mohiniyattam with Manipur and Sattriya with Kerala. Option 3 is wrong because it pairs Sattriya with Manipur and Manipuri with Assam (swapped). Option 4 is wrong because it pairs Mohiniyattam with Assam.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correctly matched (Scheme — Year of Launch)?

(i) Ayushman Bharat — 2018
(ii) Skill India Mission — 2015
(iii) Swachh Bharat Mission — 2014
(iv) PM Ujjwala Yojana — 2017

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Ayushman Bharat was launched in 2018 (i correct), Skill India in 2015 (ii correct), Swachh Bharat on 2 October 2014 (iii correct). PM Ujjwala Yojana was launched in May 2016, not 2017, making (iv) incorrect. Option 2 is wrong because (iv) is incorrect. Option 3 is wrong because it includes (iv) which has the wrong year. Option 4 is wrong because it excludes (i) which is correct and includes (iv) which is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Sardar Sarovar Dam, one of the largest dams in the world, is built on which river?
questions.explanation: Sardar Sarovar Dam is built on the river Narmada in Gujarat. Tapti is wrong — though it is a westward-flowing river in the same region, no major dam of this scale exists on it. Krishna is wrong as it flows through Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Andhra Pradesh with different dams (like Nagarjuna Sagar). Godavari is wrong as it flows eastward through central-southern India.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India:

(i) The CAG is appointed by the President of India.
(ii) The CAG can be removed only by the same procedure as a Supreme Court judge.
(iii) The CAG audits the accounts of the Central Government, State Governments, and local bodies.
(iv) The reports of the CAG are laid before Parliament by the Finance Minister.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The CAG is appointed by the President (i correct), removed by the same process as an SC judge — address by both Houses (ii correct), and audits Central, State, and local body accounts (iii correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because CAG reports are laid before Parliament by the President (not the Finance Minister), who causes them to be placed before both Houses. Option 2 is wrong because it includes (iv). Option 3 is wrong because it excludes (i) and includes (iv). Option 4 is wrong because it includes (iv).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The Indian Constitution borrowed the concept of Directive Principles of State Policy from the Constitution of __________.
questions.explanation: The Directive Principles of State Policy in Part IV of the Indian Constitution were inspired by the Irish Constitution (1937). Canada is wrong — India borrowed the federal structure with a strong Centre and residual powers from Canada. Australia is wrong — the Concurrent List and joint sitting concept came from Australia. Germany is wrong — India borrowed the concept of suspension of Fundamental Rights during an emergency from Germany (Weimar Republic).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Green Revolution in India primarily increased the production of wheat and rice.
Reason (R): The Green Revolution introduced high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds that required assured irrigation and chemical fertilizers.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution did primarily boost wheat and rice production in India (A correct). The introduction of HYV seeds requiring irrigation and fertilizers was the mechanism that enabled this increase (R correct and explains A). Option 2 is wrong because R directly explains how A was achieved. Option 3 is wrong because R is factually accurate. Option 4 is wrong because A is factually correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Konark Sun Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, was built by which ruler?
questions.explanation: The Konark Sun Temple in Odisha was built by Eastern Ganga dynasty king Narasimhadeva I in the 13th century (c. 1250 CE). Rajendra Chola I is wrong — he was a Chola king of Tamil Nadu known for naval expeditions. Krishnadevaraya is wrong — he was a Vijayanagara ruler of the 16th century associated with Hampi. Ashoka is wrong — he ruled in the 3rd century BCE, nearly 1500 years before Konark was built.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the National Commission for Scheduled Castes:

(i) It is a constitutional body established under Article 338.
(ii) Its chairperson and members are appointed by the President.
(iii) It investigates complaints relating to deprivation of rights of SCs.
(iv) It has the powers of a civil court while investigating complaints.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The NCSC is constitutional under Art. 338 (i correct), members appointed by President (ii correct), investigates complaints regarding SC rights (iii correct), and has civil court powers for investigation (iv correct). Option 1 is wrong because it excludes (iv) which is correct. Option 3 is wrong because it excludes (ii). Option 4 is wrong because it excludes (i).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following Five-Year Plans with their primary focus:

Column I:
(a) First Five-Year Plan (1951-56)
(b) Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61)
(c) Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-74)
(d) Eighth Five-Year Plan (1992-97)

Column II:
(i) Liberalization and market-oriented reforms
(ii) Agriculture and irrigation
(iii) Heavy industries (Mahalanobis Model)
(iv) Growth with stability

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: The First Plan focused on agriculture and irrigation (ii), the Second Plan on heavy industries under the Mahalanobis Model (iii), the Fourth Plan on growth with stability (iv), and the Eighth Plan on liberalization and market reforms following 1991 reforms (i). Option 2 is wrong as it swaps First and Second Plan focuses. Option 3 is wrong as it assigns heavy industries to the Fourth Plan. Option 4 is wrong as it assigns growth with stability to the First Plan.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Strait of Palk separates India from which country?
questions.explanation: The Palk Strait lies between Tamil Nadu (India) and northern Sri Lanka. Maldives is wrong — it is an island nation far southwest of India in the Indian Ocean, not separated by a strait. Myanmar is wrong — India and Myanmar are separated by land borders and the Andaman Sea. Bangladesh is wrong — it shares a land border with India with no separating strait.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are functions of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)?

(i) Issuing currency notes
(ii) Acting as the banker to the Government
(iii) Fixing the repo rate and reverse repo rate
(iv) Regulating the stock exchanges in India

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: RBI issues currency (i correct), acts as banker to governments (ii correct), and sets repo/reverse repo rates as part of monetary policy (iii correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because stock exchanges in India are regulated by SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India), not RBI. Option 2 is wrong because it includes (iv). Option 3 is wrong because it includes (iv) and excludes (ii). Option 4 is wrong because it excludes (i) and includes (iv).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The monsoon winds in India reverse their direction between summer and winter.
Reason (R): The differential heating and cooling of land and sea causes a seasonal shift in pressure zones, reversing wind patterns.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Indian monsoon winds do reverse seasonally — southwest in summer, northeast in winter (A correct). This reversal is caused by differential heating/cooling of land and sea creating seasonal pressure shifts (R correct and directly explains A). Option 2 is wrong because R is the precise mechanism explaining A. Option 3 is wrong because R is scientifically accurate. Option 4 is wrong because A is factually correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Indira Point, the southernmost tip of Indian territory, is located in which island group?
questions.explanation: Indira Point (formerly Pygmalion Point) in Great Nicobar Island is India's southernmost point. Lakshadweep is wrong — these islands are in the Arabian Sea, west of Kerala, and not India's southernmost point. Diu Island is wrong — it is off Gujarat coast in western India. Rameshwaram Islands is wrong — Rameshwaram is in Tamil Nadu and is near (but not) the southernmost mainland point, not the southernmost territory.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Election Commission of India:

(i) It is a permanent constitutional body established under Article 324.
(ii) The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed only through impeachment.
(iii) The Election Commission conducts elections to the Panchayats and Municipalities.
(iv) It prepares and revises the electoral rolls.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: ECI is constitutional under Art. 324 (i correct) and prepares/revises electoral rolls (iv correct). Statement (ii) is wrong because the CEC is removed by the same process as a Supreme Court judge (address by Parliament), which is technically different from 'impeachment' — impeachment applies only to the President. Statement (iii) is wrong because Panchayat and Municipality elections are conducted by the State Election Commissions, not the ECI. Option 2 is wrong because (ii) is incorrect. Option 3 is wrong because (iii) is incorrect. Option 4 is wrong because both (ii) and (iii) are incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Kartarpur Corridor', opened in November 2019, connects which two countries?
questions.explanation: The Kartarpur Corridor connects Dera Baba Nanak (India) to Gurdwara Darbar Sahib Kartarpur (Pakistan) for Sikh pilgrims. India and Bangladesh is wrong — there is no corridor by this name between these countries. India and Nepal is wrong — pilgrim routes to Nepal are not called Kartarpur Corridor. India and Myanmar is wrong — no such corridor exists between these nations.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following national parks with the states they are located in:

Column I:
(a) Kaziranga National Park
(b) Periyar National Park
(c) Ranthambore National Park
(d) Hemis National Park

Column II:
(i) Rajasthan
(ii) Ladakh
(iii) Assam
(iv) Kerala

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Kaziranga is in Assam (iii) known for one-horned rhinoceros, Periyar in Kerala (iv) known for elephants, Ranthambore in Rajasthan (i) known for tigers, and Hemis in Ladakh (ii) known for snow leopards. Option 2 swaps most pairings. Option 3 wrongly pairs Periyar with Rajasthan. Option 4 wrongly pairs Kaziranga with Ladakh.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The NITI Aayog replaced which earlier body in January 2015?
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) was established on 1 January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission which had existed since 1950. National Development Council is wrong — it continues to exist as a separate body. Finance Commission is wrong — it is a constitutional body under Art. 280 that still functions independently. University Grants Commission is wrong — UGC deals with higher education and was not replaced.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India is the world's largest producer of milk.
Reason (R): Operation Flood, launched by Dr. Verghese Kurien, transformed India into a milk-surplus nation through dairy cooperatives.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: India is indeed the world's largest milk producer (A correct). Operation Flood, spearheaded by Dr. Verghese Kurien and launched in 1970, created a national milk grid through cooperatives like Amul, which is the direct reason India became a milk-surplus nation (R correct and explains A). Option 2 is wrong because R directly explains how India achieved the position stated in A. Option 3 is wrong because R is factually accurate. Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Bhakra Nangal Dam, one of the highest gravity dams in the world, is built on which river?
questions.explanation: Bhakra Nangal Dam is constructed on the river Sutlej in Bilaspur, Himachal Pradesh. Beas is wrong — the Pong Dam and Pandoh Dam are on the Beas. Ravi is wrong — the Ranjit Sagar Dam is on the Ravi. Chenab is wrong — the Salal Dam and Baglihar Dam are on the Chenab.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India:

(i) GST was implemented from 1 July 2017.
(ii) The GST Council is a constitutional body under Article 279A.
(iii) GST subsumed multiple indirect taxes including excise duty, VAT, and service tax.
(iv) Petroleum products are fully covered under GST since its inception.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: GST was implemented on 1 July 2017 (i correct), the GST Council is constitutional under Art. 279A (ii correct), and it subsumed excise, VAT, service tax, etc. (iii correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because petroleum products (crude oil, petrol, diesel, ATF, natural gas) are kept outside GST and continue to be taxed under the old regime. Option 2 includes (iv) which is wrong. Option 3 includes (iv) and excludes (ii). Option 4 excludes (i) and includes (iv).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The __________ is the highest civilian award given by the Government of India.
questions.explanation: Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian honour, recognizing exceptional service of the highest order. Padma Vibhushan is wrong — it is the second-highest civilian award. Padma Bhushan is wrong — it is the third-highest. Padma Shri is wrong — it is the fourth-highest civilian award.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Simon Commission, which visited India in 1928, was boycotted because:
options: It proposed the partition of India
It recommended abolition of provincial autonomy
It increased the tax burden on Indians
questions.explanation: The Simon Commission (1927-28) was boycotted by Indians because all seven members were British — there was no Indian representation. 'It proposed the partition of India' is wrong because partition was proposed much later. 'It recommended abolition of provincial autonomy' is wrong — the Commission actually recommended abolition of diarchy. 'It increased the tax burden on Indians' is wrong — the Commission dealt with constitutional reforms, not taxation.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Brahmaputra river causes severe flooding in Assam almost every year.
Reason (R): The Brahmaputra carries a huge volume of water and sediment from steep Himalayan slopes, and its channel becomes shallower and braided in the Assam plains.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: The Brahmaputra does cause annual flooding in Assam (A correct). The river carries enormous sediment from the Himalayas, reducing channel depth and creating a braided pattern in the plains, which leads to overflow during monsoons (R correct and explains A). Option 2 is wrong because R is the direct geomorphological explanation for the flooding. Option 3 is wrong because R is scientifically accurate. Option 4 is wrong because A is factually correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The headquarters of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) is located at:
questions.explanation: The ICJ (principal judicial organ of the UN) is headquartered at the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands. Geneva is wrong — WHO and WTO are headquartered there, not the ICJ. New York is wrong — the UN headquarters and General Assembly are there. Vienna is wrong — the IAEA and UNIDO are headquartered there.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are Fundamental Duties under Article 51A of the Indian Constitution?

(i) To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals
(ii) To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood
(iii) To vote in every election
(iv) To protect and improve the natural environment

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Abiding by the Constitution (i), promoting brotherhood (ii), and protecting the environment (iv) are all listed in Art. 51A. Statement (iii) is wrong because voting in elections is NOT listed as a Fundamental Duty — it is a right, not a constitutional duty under Art. 51A. Option 2 includes (iii) which is wrong. Option 3 includes (iii) and excludes (ii). Option 4 excludes (i) and includes (iii).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Nalanda University ruins, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, are located in which state?
questions.explanation: The ruins of Nalanda Mahavihara (ancient Buddhist university) are in Rajgir area of Bihar. Uttar Pradesh is wrong — though it has Sarnath and other Buddhist sites, Nalanda is in Bihar. Madhya Pradesh is wrong — it has Sanchi Stupa but not Nalanda. Odisha is wrong — it has Konark and other heritage sites but not Nalanda.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following international organizations with their founding years:

Column I:
(a) World Trade Organization (WTO)
(b) International Monetary Fund (IMF)
(c) ASEAN
(d) African Union (AU)

Column II:
(i) 1945
(ii) 1967
(iii) 1995
(iv) 2002

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: WTO was established in 1995 (iii), IMF in 1945 at Bretton Woods (i), ASEAN in 1967 by the Bangkok Declaration (ii), and the African Union in 2002 replacing the OAU (iv). Option 2 wrongly assigns IMF to 1995 and WTO to 1945. Option 3 assigns IMF to 1967 and ASEAN to 1945. Option 4 assigns WTO to 2002.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Right to Information (RTI) Act was enacted in India in which year?
questions.explanation: The RTI Act was passed by Parliament in 2005 and came into effect on 12 October 2005. 2003 is wrong — the Freedom of Information Act was passed in 2002 but was replaced by RTI. 2007 is wrong — by then RTI was already operational. 2001 is wrong — no such legislation existed at the Central level then.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO):

(i) ISRO's headquarters is located in Bengaluru.
(ii) Chandrayaan-3 achieved a soft landing near the Moon's south pole in August 2023.
(iii) The Satish Dhawan Space Centre is located in Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh.
(iv) ISRO was founded in 1959 by Dr. Vikram Sarabhai.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: ISRO HQ is in Bengaluru (i correct), Chandrayaan-3 landed near the south pole on 23 Aug 2023 (ii correct), and Sriharikota is in Andhra Pradesh (iii correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because ISRO was established in 1969. The Indian National Committee for Space Research (INCOSPAR) was founded in 1962 (not 1959) by Vikram Sarabhai, and ISRO replaced INCOSPAR in 1969. Option 2 includes (iv). Option 3 excludes (ii) and includes (iv). Option 4 excludes (i) and includes (iv).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows India's medal tally at the 2024 Paris Olympics:

| Medal Type | Count |
|---|---|
| Gold | 0 |
| Silver | 1 |
| Bronze | 5 |

What was India's total medal count at the 2024 Paris Olympics?
questions.explanation: India won 0 Gold + 1 Silver + 5 Bronze = 6 medals total at Paris 2024. Option '5' is wrong — it counts only bronze medals. Option '7' is wrong — there is no additional medal to account for. Option '8' is wrong — it overestimates the tally.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following rivers does NOT originate in India?

(i) Brahmaputra
(ii) Sutlej
(iii) Ganga
(iv) Indus

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Brahmaputra originates in Tibet (Angsi Glacier) (i correct), Sutlej originates near Lake Rakshastal in Tibet (ii correct), and Indus originates near Lake Mansarovar in Tibet (iv correct). Ganga originates at Gangotri Glacier in Uttarakhand, India, so (iii) is incorrect — it does originate in India. Option 2 is wrong because it excludes (iv) — the Indus also originates in Tibet. Option 3 excludes (ii). Option 4 includes (iii) which is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Poona Pact of 1932 was an agreement between Mahatma Gandhi and:
questions.explanation: The Poona Pact (1932) was signed between Gandhi and Ambedkar, resolving the dispute over separate electorates for depressed classes by providing reserved seats within joint electorates. Jinnah is wrong — he was involved in Hindu-Muslim matters, not the depressed classes issue. Nehru is wrong — he was not a party to the Poona Pact. Bose is wrong — he was not involved in this agreement.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY):

(i) It aims to provide affordable housing to the urban and rural poor.
(ii) Under PMAY-Urban, the beneficiary gets interest subsidy on home loans.
(iii) PMAY was launched in June 2015.
(iv) Only below-poverty-line (BPL) families are eligible for PMAY benefits.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: PMAY targets both urban and rural poor for housing (i correct), provides Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme under PMAY-U (ii correct), and was launched in June 2015 (iii correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because PMAY covers EWS, LIG, and MIG categories — not exclusively BPL families. Option 2 includes (iv). Option 3 excludes (ii) and includes (iv). Option 4 excludes (i) and includes (iv).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Tropic of Cancer passes through eight Indian states.
Reason (R): India extends from approximately 8°N to 37°N latitude, placing the Tropic of Cancer (23.5°N) roughly through the middle of the country.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer does pass through eight states (Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, Mizoram) (A correct). India's latitudinal extent places 23.5°N through the middle (R correct). However, R explains WHY the Tropic passes through India, not WHY it passes through exactly eight states — the number depends on state boundaries, not India's latitudinal extent. Option 1 is wrong because R doesn't explain the specific number 'eight'. Option 3 is wrong because R is factually correct. Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The term 'Fourth Estate' refers to:
questions.explanation: The 'Fourth Estate' is a term traditionally used to refer to the press or news media, considered the fourth pillar of democracy. The Judiciary is wrong — it is the third branch of government (executive, legislature, judiciary). The Civil Services is wrong — they are the bureaucracy, not called the Fourth Estate. The Military is wrong — armed forces are not referred to by this term.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following centrally sponsored schemes with their objectives:

Column I:
(a) PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana
(b) Jal Jeevan Mission
(c) PM SVANidhi
(d) Ayushman Bharat

Column II:
(i) Affordable credit to street vendors
(ii) Free food grain distribution to poor
(iii) Health insurance coverage of ₹5 lakh per family
(iv) Tap water connection to every rural household

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: PM-GKAY distributes free food grains (ii), Jal Jeevan Mission aims for tap water to rural households (iv), PM SVANidhi provides micro-credit to street vendors (i), and Ayushman Bharat provides ₹5 lakh health cover (iii). Option 2 pairs GKAY with tap water and JJM with food. Option 3 pairs JJM with street vendors. Option 4 pairs GKAY with health insurance.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Ajanta and Ellora caves are located in which state of India?
questions.explanation: Both Ajanta and Ellora caves are located in the Aurangabad district (now Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar) of Maharashtra. Madhya Pradesh is wrong — it has Bhimbetka rock shelters but not Ajanta/Ellora. Karnataka is wrong — it has Badami and Aihole caves. Rajasthan is wrong — it has Dilwara temples but not these caves.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about India's nuclear doctrine:

(i) India follows a 'No First Use' (NFU) policy for nuclear weapons.
(ii) India conducted its first nuclear test (Smiling Buddha) in 1974 at Pokhran.
(iii) The Nuclear Command Authority is chaired by the Prime Minister.
(iv) India is a signatory to the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT).

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: India has an NFU policy (i correct), conducted Pokhran-I in 1974 (ii correct), and the NCA is chaired by the PM (iii correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because India has NOT signed the NPT, considering it discriminatory between nuclear-weapon states and others. Option 2 includes (iv). Option 3 excludes (ii) and includes (iv). Option 4 excludes (i) and includes (iv).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows India's top exports by value in FY 2023-24:

| Sector | Share in Total Exports |
|---|---|
| Petroleum Products | 17% |
| Gems & Jewellery | 8% |
| Pharmaceuticals | 6% |
| Engineering Goods | 25% |
| Textiles & Apparel | 10% |

Based on the data, what is the combined share of Petroleum Products and Engineering Goods in India's total exports?
questions.explanation: Petroleum Products (17%) + Engineering Goods (25%) = 42%. Option '35%' is wrong — it would be 17+18, not the correct calculation. Option '33%' is wrong — it would be 8+25, combining the wrong sectors. Option '47%' is wrong — it adds an extra sector's share.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Doctrine of Lapse' was introduced by which Governor-General of India?
questions.explanation: The Doctrine of Lapse was introduced by Lord Dalhousie (Governor-General 1848-56) to annex princely states without natural heirs. Lord Wellesley is wrong — he introduced the Subsidiary Alliance system. Lord Cornwallis is wrong — he introduced the Permanent Settlement (1793). Lord Hastings is wrong — he was associated with expansion but not this doctrine.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the area (in lakh sq km) under major crops in India:

| Crop | Area (lakh sq km) |
|---|---|
| Rice | 4.4 |
| Wheat | 3.1 |
| Pulses | 2.8 |
| Oilseeds | 2.5 |
| Cotton | 1.2 |

Which crop occupies the largest area under cultivation according to the data?
questions.explanation: From the data, Rice has the highest area at 4.4 lakh sq km. Wheat is wrong — it has 3.1, less than Rice. Pulses is wrong — 2.8 is third highest. Oilseeds is wrong — 2.5 is fourth highest.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides for the establishment of a Finance Commission?
questions.explanation: Article 280 provides for the constitution of a Finance Commission every five years (or earlier) to recommend distribution of tax revenues between Centre and states. Article 300A is wrong — it deals with the right to property. Article 324 is wrong — it deals with the Election Commission. Article 352 is wrong — it deals with the proclamation of national emergency.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following statements about India's steel industry are correct?

(i) India is the second-largest producer of crude steel in the world.
(ii) SAIL (Steel Authority of India Ltd) is the largest steel producer in India.
(iii) Jamshedpur has India's oldest private-sector steel plant (TISCO, now Tata Steel).
(iv) The National Steel Policy 2017 targets 300 million tonnes capacity by 2030-31.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: India is the world's second-largest crude steel producer (i correct), TISCO in Jamshedpur (1907) is India's oldest private steel plant (iii correct), and NSP 2017 targets 300 MT by 2030-31 (iv correct). Statement (ii) is wrong because Tata Steel (including its global operations) has a larger production capacity than SAIL. Option 2 includes (ii) and excludes (iv). Option 3 includes (ii). Option 4 excludes (i) and includes (ii).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The ancient city of Harappa, one of the key sites of the Indus Valley Civilization, is located in present-day:
questions.explanation: Harappa is located in the Punjab province of present-day Pakistan (Sahiwal district). India is wrong — though Mohenjo-daro's twin city, Harappa itself is across the border. Afghanistan is wrong — no Indus Valley sites of this significance exist there. Bangladesh is wrong — it is in eastern South Asia, far from the Indus basin.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):

(i) The SDGs were adopted by the United Nations in 2015.
(ii) There are 17 Sustainable Development Goals.
(iii) The target year for achieving the SDGs is 2030.
(iv) SDG 1 is 'Zero Hunger'.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: SDGs were adopted in 2015 (i correct), there are 17 goals (ii correct), and the target year is 2030 (iii correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because SDG 1 is 'No Poverty' — 'Zero Hunger' is SDG 2. Option 2 includes (iv). Option 3 excludes (ii) and includes (iv). Option 4 excludes (i) and includes (iv).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Indian Independence Act 1947' was passed by the British Parliament on:
questions.explanation: The Indian Independence Act received Royal Assent on 18 July 1947. 15 August 1947 is wrong — that is the date India actually gained independence, not when the Act was passed. 3 June 1947 is wrong — that was when the Mountbatten Plan (partition plan) was announced, before the Act was drafted. 26 January 1947 is wrong — that date in 1950 marks Republic Day, and in 1930 was Purna Swaraj Day.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following rivers with the dams built on them:

Column I:
(a) Hirakud Dam
(b) Tehri Dam
(c) Nagarjuna Sagar Dam
(d) Mettur Dam

Column II:
(i) Krishna
(ii) Mahanadi
(iii) Bhagirathi
(iv) Kaveri

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Hirakud Dam is on Mahanadi (ii) in Odisha, Tehri Dam on Bhagirathi (iii) in Uttarakhand, Nagarjuna Sagar on Krishna (i) in Telangana, and Mettur Dam on Kaveri (iv) in Tamil Nadu. Option 2 wrongly pairs Hirakud with Bhagirathi and Tehri with Mahanadi. Option 3 pairs Tehri with Kaveri. Option 4 pairs Hirakud with Krishna.
